ugens.name: MoogFF
ugens.doc: A digital implementation of the Moog VCF (filter).

args.name: gain
args.doc: The filter resonance gain, between zero and 4

args.name: reset
args.doc: When greater than zero, this will reset the state of the digital filters at the beginning of a computational block.

ugens.name: PartConv
ugens.doc: Partitioned convolution. Various additional buffers must be supplied. Mono impulse response only! If inputting multiple channels, you'll need independent PartConvs, one for each channel. But the charm is: impulse response can be as large as you like (CPU load increases with IR size. Various tradeoffs based on fftsize choice, due to rarer but larger FFTs. This plug-in uses amortisation to spread processing and avoid spikes). Normalisation factors difficult to anticipate; convolution piles up multiple copies of the input on top of itself, so can easily overload.

args.name: fftsize
args.doc: Spectral convolution partition size (twice partition size). You must ensure that the blocksize divides the partition size and there are at least two blocks per partition (to allow for amortisation)

args.name: irbufnum
args.doc: Prepared buffer of spectra for each partition of the inpulse response

ugens.name: PitchShift
ugens.doc: A time domain granular pitch shifter. Grains have a triangular amplitude envelope and an overlap of 4:1.

args.name: windowSize
args.doc: The size of the grain window in seconds. This value cannot be modulated.

args.name: pitchRatio
args.doc: The ratio of the pitch shift. Must be from 0.0 to 4.0

args.name: pitchDispersion
args.doc: The maximum random deviation of the pitch from the pitchRatio.

args.name: timeDispersion
args.doc: A random offset of from zero to timeDispersion seconds is added to the delay of each grain. Use of some dispersion can alleviate a hard comb filter effect due to uniform grain placement. It can also be an effect in itself. timeDispersion can be no larger than windowSize.

ugens.name: Pluck
ugens.doc: Implements the Karplus-Strong style of synthesis, where a delay line (normally starting with noise) is filtered and fed back on itself so that over time it becomes periodic.

args.name: trig
args.doc: Upon a negative to positive transition, the excitation signal will be fed into the delay line.

args.name: maxdelaytime
args.doc: The max delay time in seconds (initializes the internal delay buffer).

args.name: decaytime
args.doc: Time for the echoes to decay by 60 decibels. Negative times emphasize odd partials.

args.name: coef
args.doc: The coef of the internal OnePole filter. Values should be between -1 and +1 (larger values will be unstable... so be careful!).

ugens.name: Spring
ugens.doc: Physical model of resonating spring

ugens.name: TBall
ugens.doc: models the impacts of a bouncing object that is reflected by a vibrating surface

args.name: friction
args.doc: proximity from which on attraction to surface starts

ugens.name: BrownNoise
ugens.summary: Noise whose spectrum falls off in power by 6 dB per octave.
ugens.doc: Useful for generating percussive sounds such as snares and hand claps. Also useful for simulating wind or sea effects, for producing breath effects in wind instrument timbres or for producing the typical trance leads.

ugens.name: ClipNoise
ugens.summary: Noise whose values are either -1 or 1.
ugens.doc: This produces the maximum energy for the least peak to peak amplitude. Useful for generating percussive sounds such as snares and hand claps. Also useful for simulating wind or sea effects, for producing breath effects in wind instrument timbres or for producing the typical trance leads.

ugens.name: Crackle
ugens.summary: Chaotic noise generator
ugens.doc: A noise generator based on a chaotic function. Useful for generating percussive sounds such as snares and hand claps. Also useful for simulating wind or sea effects, for producing breath effects in wind instrument timbres or for producing the typical trance leads.

args.name: chaosParam
args.doc: a parameter of the chaotic function with useful values from just below 1.0 to just above 2.0. Towards 2.0 the sound crackles.

ugens.name: Dust
ugens.doc: Generates random impulses from 0 to +1.

args.name: density
args.doc: average number of impulses per second

ugens.name: Dust2
ugens.doc: Generates random impulses from -1 to +1.

args.name: density
args.doc: average number of impulses per second.

ugens.name: GrayNoise
ugens.summary: Random impulses from -1 to +1 given a density
ugens.doc: Creates a sequence of random impulses from -1 to +1. Generates noise which results from flipping random bits in a word. This type of noise has a high RMS level relative to its peak to peak level. The spectrum is emphasized towards lower frequencies. Useful for generating percussive sounds such as snares and hand claps. Also useful for simulating wind or sea effects, for producing breath effects in wind instrument timbres or for producing the typical trance leads.

ugens.name: Hasher
ugens.doc: Returns a unique output value from zero to one for each input value according to a hash function. The same input value will always produce the same output value. The input need not be from zero to one.

ugens.name: LFClipNoise
ugens.doc: Randomly generates the values -1 or +1 at a rate given by the nearest integer division of the sample rate by the freq argument. It is probably pretty hard on your speakers!

args.name: freq
args.doc: approximate rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: LFDClipNoise
ugens.doc: Like lf-clip-noise, it generates the values -1 or +1 at a rate given by the freq argument, with two differences: * no time quantization * fast recovery from low freq values. (lf-clip-noise, as well as lf-noise0,1,2 quantize to the nearest integer division of the samplerate, and they poll the freq argument only when scheduled; thus they often seem to hang when freqs get very low). If you don't need very high or very low freqs, or use fixed freqs lf-noise0 is more efficient.

args.name: freq
args.doc: rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: LFDNoise0
ugens.doc: Like lf-noise0, it generates random values between -1 and 1 at a rate given by the freq argument, with two differences: p * no time quantization * fast recovery from low freq values. (lf-noise0,1,2 quantize to the nearest integer division of the samplerate and they poll the freq argument only when scheduled, and thus seem to hang when freqs get very low). If you don't need very high or very low freqs, or use fixed freqs lf-noise0 is more efficient.

args.name: freq
args.doc: rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: LFDNoise1
ugens.doc: Like lf-noise1, it generates linearly interpolated random values between -1 and 1 at a rate given by the freq argument, with two differences: * no time quantization * fast recovery from low freq values. (lf-noise0,1,2 quantize to the nearest integer division of the samplerate and they poll the freq argument only when scheduled, and thus seem to hang when freqs get very low). If you don't need very high or very low freqs, or use fixed freqs lf-noise1 is more efficient.

args.name: freq
args.doc: rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: LFDNoise3
ugens.doc: Similar to lf-noise2, it generates polynomially interpolated random values between -1 and 1 at a rate given by the freq argument, with 3 differences: * no time quantization * fast recovery from low freq values * cubic instead of quadratic interpolation (lf-noise0,1,2 quantize to the nearest integer division of the samplerate and they poll the freq argument only when scheduled, and thus seem to hang when freqs get very low). If you don't need very high or very low freqs, or use fixed freqs lf-noise2 is more efficient.

args.name: freq
args.doc: rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: LFNoise0
ugens.doc: Generates random values between -1 and 1 at a rate (the rate is not guaranteed but approximate)

args.name: freq
args.doc: approximate rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: LFNoise1
ugens.doc: Generates linearly interpolated random values between -1 and 1 at the supplied rate (the rate is not guaranteed but approximate).

args.name: freq
args.doc: approximate rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: LFNoise2
ugens.doc: Generates quadratically interpolated random values between -1 and 1 at the supplied rate (the rate is not guaranteed but approximate). Note: quadratic interpolation means that the noise values can occasionally extend beyond the normal range of +-1, if the freq varies in certain ways. If this is undesirable then you might like to clip2 the values or use a linearly-interpolating unit instead.

args.name: freq
args.doc: approximate rate at which to generate random values.

ugens.name: Logistic
ugens.doc: A noise generator based on the logistic map: y = chaos-param * y * (1.0 - y) y will stay in the range of 0.0 to 1.0 for normal values of the chaos-param. This leads to a DC offset and may cause a pop when you stop the Synth. For output you might want to combine this UGen with a LeakDC or rescale around 0.0 via mul and add: see example below.

args.name: chaosParam
args.doc: a parameter of the chaotic function with useful values from 0.0 to 4.0. Chaos occurs from 3.57 up. Don't use values outside this range if you don't want the UGen to blow up.

args.name: freq
args.doc: Frequency of calculation; if over the sampling rate, this is clamped to the sampling rate

args.name: init
args.doc: Initial value of y (see equation below)

ugens.name: MantissaMask
ugens.doc: Masks off bits in the mantissa of the floating point sample value. This introduces a quantization noise, but is less severe than linearly quantizing the signal.

args.name: bits
args.doc: the number of mantissa bits to preserve. a number from 0 to 23.

ugens.name: PinkNoise
ugens.summary: Noise whose spectrum falls off in power by 3 dB per octave.
ugens.doc: Noise that gives equal power over the span of each octave. Useful for generating percussive sounds such as snares and hand claps. Also useful for simulating wind or sea effects, for producing breath effects in wind instrument timbres or for producing the typical trance leads. This version gives 8 octaves of pink noise.

ugens.name: WhiteNoise
ugens.summary: Noise whose spectrum has equal power at all frequencies.
ugens.doc: Noise that contains equal amounts of energy at every frequency - comparable to radio static. Useful for generating percussive sounds such as snares and hand claps. Also useful for simulating wind or sea effects, for producing breath effects in wind instrument timbres or for producing the typical trance leads.

ugens.name: COsc
ugens.doc: Chorusing wavetable lookup oscillator. Produces sum of two signals at (freq +/- (beats / 2)). Due to summing, the peak amplitude is twice that of the wavetable.

args.name: bufnum
args.doc: The number of a buffer filled in wavetable format

ugens.name: DegreeToKey
ugens.doc: the input signal value is truncated to an integer value and used as an index into an octave repeating table of note values (indices wrap around the table)

args.name: bufnum
args.doc: Index of the buffer which contains the steps for each scale degree.

args.name: octave
args.doc: The number of steps per octave in the scale. The default is 12.

ugens.name: DetectIndex
ugens.doc: search a buffer for a value

ugens.name: Formant
ugens.doc: Generates a set of harmonics around a formant frequency at a given fundamental frequency. The frequency inputs are read at control rate only, so if you use an audio rate UGen as an input, it will only be sampled at the start of each audio synthesis block.

args.name: bwfreq
args.doc: Pulse width frequency in Hertz. Controls the bandwidth of the formant (control rate)

ugens.name: Impulse
ugens.doc: non band limited impulse oscillator. Outputs a single 1 every freq cycles per second and 0 the rest of the time.

ugens.name: Index
ugens.doc: the input signal value is truncated to an integer and used as an index into the table

ugens.name: IndexInBetween
ugens.doc: finds the (lowest) point in the buffer at which the input signal lies in-between the two values, and returns the index

ugens.name: LFCub
ugens.doc: an oscillator outputting a sine like shape made of two cubic pieces

args.name: iphase
args.doc: Initial phase offset. For efficiency reasons this is a value ranging from 0 to 2.

ugens.name: LFGauss
ugens.doc: A non-band-limited gaussian function oscillator. Output ranges from minval to 1. LFGauss implements the formula: f(x) = exp(squared(x - iphase) / (-2.0 * squared(width))) where x is to vary in the range -1 to 1 over the period dur. minval is the initial value at -1

args.name: duration
args.doc: Duration of one full cycle ( for freq input: dur = 1 / freq )

args.name: width
args.doc: Relative width of the bell. Best to keep below 0.25 when used as envelope.

args.name: loop
args.doc: If loop is > 0, UGen oscillates. Otherwise it calls the done action after one cycle

args.name: action
args.doc: Action to be evaluated after cycle completes. Default: NO-ACTION.

ugens.name: LFPar
ugens.doc: a non band-limited parabolic oscillator outputing a high of 1 and a low of zero.

args.name: iphase
args.doc: Initial phase offset. For efficiency reasons this is a value ranging from 0 to 2.

ugens.name: LFPulse
ugens.doc: A non-band-limited pulse oscillator. Outputs a high value of one and a low value of zero.

args.name: width
args.doc: Pulse width duty cycle from zero to one

ugens.name: LFSaw
ugens.doc: low freq (i.e. not band limited) sawtooth oscillator

args.name: iphase
args.doc: Initial phase offset. For efficiency reasons this is a value ranging from 0 to 2.

ugens.name: LFTri
ugens.summary: a non-band-limited triangle oscillator
ugens.doc: The triangle wave shape features two linear slopes and is not as harmonically rich as a sawtooth wave since it only contains odd harmonics (partials). Ideally, this type of wave form is mixed with a sine, square or pulse wave to add a sparkling or bright effect to a sound and is often employed on pads to give them a glittery feel.

args.name: iphase
args.doc: Initial phase offset. For efficiency reasons this is a value ranging from 0 to 2.

ugens.name: Osc
ugens.doc: Linear interpolating wavetable lookup oscillator with frequency and phase modulation inputs. This oscillator requires a buffer to be filled with a wavetable format signal. This preprocesses the Signal into a form which can be used efficiently by the Oscillator. The buffer size must be a power of 2. This can be achieved by creating a Buffer object and sending it one of the b_gen messages (sine1, sine2, sine3) with the wavetable flag set to true. This can also be achieved by creating a Signal object and sending it the 'asWavetable' message, saving it to disk, and having the server load it from there.

args.name: phase
args.doc: Phase offset or modulator in radians

ugens.name: Select
ugens.doc: select the output signal from an array of inputs

args.name: channelsArray
args.doc: List of ugens to choose from

ugens.name: Shaper
ugens.doc: performs waveshaping on the input signal by indexing into a table

ugens.name: SinOsc
ugens.summary: Sine table lookup oscillator
ugens.doc: Outputs a sine wave with values oscillating between -1 and 1 similar to osc except that the table has already been fixed as a sine table of 8192 entries. Sine waves are often used for creating sub-basses or are mixed with other waveforms to add extra body or bottom end to a sound. They contain no harmonics and consist entirely of the fundamental frequency. This means that they're not suitable for subtractive synthesis i.e. passing through filters such as a hpf or lpf. However, they are useful for additive synthesis i.e. adding multiple sine waves together at different frequencies, amplitudes and phase to create new timbres.

args.name: phase
args.doc: Phase offset or modulator in radians

ugens.name: SinOscFB
ugens.summary: Sine oscillator with phase modulation feedback
ugens.doc: Different feedback values results in a modulation between a sine wave and a sawtooth like wave. Overmodulation causes chaotic oscillation.

args.name: feedback
args.doc: amplitude of phase feedback in radians

ugens.name: SyncSaw
ugens.summary: hard sync sawtooth wave oscillator
ugens.doc: A sawtooth wave that is hard synched to a fundamental pitch. This produces an effect similar to moving formants or pulse width modulation. The sawtooth oscillator has its phase reset when the sync oscillator completes a cycle. This is not a band limited waveform, so it may alias.

args.name: sawFreq
args.doc: Frequency of the slave synched sawtooth wave. saw-freq should always be greater than sync-freq.

ugens.name: VOsc
ugens.doc: A wavetable lookup oscillator which can be swept smoothly across wavetables. All the wavetables must be allocated to the same size. Fractional values of table will interpolate between two adjacent tables. This oscillator requires at least two buffers to be filled with a wavetable format signal. This preprocesses the Signal into a form which can be used efficiently by the Oscillator. The buffer size must be a power of 2.

args.name: bufpos
args.doc: Buffer index. Can be swept continuously among adjacent wavetable buffers of the same size.

args.name: phase
args.doc: Phase offset of modulator in radians

ugens.name: VOsc3
ugens.doc: Three variable wavetable oscillators. A wavetable lookup oscillator which can be swept smoothly across wavetables. All the wavetables must be allocated to the same size. Fractional values of table will interpolate between two adjacent tables. This unit generator contains three oscillators at different frequencies, mixed together. This oscillator requires at least two buffers to be filled with a wavetable format signal. This preprocesses the Signal into a form which can be used efficiently by the Oscillator. The buffer size must be a power of 2.

args.name: bufpos
args.doc: Buffer index. Can be swept continuously among adjacent wavetable buffers of the same size.

args.name: freq1
args.doc: Frequency in Hertz of first oscillator

args.name: freq2
args.doc: Frequency in Hertz of second oscillator

args.name: freq3
args.doc: Frequency in Hertz of third oscillator

ugens.name: VarSaw
ugens.doc: a variable duty cycle saw wave oscillator

args.name: width
args.doc: Duty cycle from zero to one. (0 = downward sawtooth, 0.5 = triangle, 1 = upward sawtooth)

ugens.name: Vibrato
ugens.summary: Models a slow frequency modulation.
ugens.doc: Vibrato is a slow frequency modulation. Consider the systematic deviation in pitch of a singer around a fundamental frequency, or a violinist whose finger wobbles in position on the fingerboard, slightly tightening and loosening the string to add shimmer to the pitch. There is often also a delay before vibrato is established on a note. This UGen models these processes; by setting more extreme settings, you can get back to the timbres of FM synthesis. You can also add in some noise to the vibrato rate and vibrato size (modulation depth) to make for a more realistic motor pattern. The vibrato output is a waveform based on a squared envelope shape with four stages marking out 0.0 to 1.0, 1.0 to 0.0, 0.0 to -1.0, and -1.0 back to 0.0. Vibrato rate determines how quickly you move through these stages.

args.name: freq
args.doc: Fundamental frequency in Hertz. If the Vibrato UGen is running at audio rate, this must not be a constant, but an actual audio rate UGen

args.name: rate
args.doc: Vibrato rate, speed of wobble in Hertz. Note that if this is set to a low value (and definitely with 0.0), you may never get vibrato back, since the rate input is only checked at the end of a cycle.

args.name: depth
args.doc: Size of vibrato frequency deviation around the fundamental, as a proportion of the fundamental. 0.02 = 2% of the fundamental.

args.name: delay
args.doc: Delay before vibrato is established in seconds (a singer tends to attack a note and then stabilise with vibrato, for instance).

args.name: onset
args.doc: Transition time in seconds from no vibrato to full vibrato after the initial delay time.

args.name: rateVariation
args.doc: Noise on the rate, expressed as a proportion of the rate; can change once per cycle of vibrato.

args.name: depthVariation
args.doc: Noise on the depth of modulation, expressed as a proportion of the depth; can change once per cycle of vibrato. The noise affects independently the up and the down part of vibrato shape within a cycle.

args.name: iphase
args.doc: Initial phase of vibrato modulation, allowing starting above or below the fundamental rather than on it.

ugens.name: WrapIndex
ugens.doc: the input signal value is truncated to an integer value and used as an index into the table (out of range index values are wrapped)

ugens.name: Balance2
ugens.doc: Equal power panning balances two channels; by panning, you are favouring one or other channel in the mix, and the other loses power. The middle pan position (pos=0.0) corresponds to the original stereo mix; full left (pos of -1) is essentially just left channel playing, full right (pos of 1) just the right. The output of Balance2 remains a stereo signal.

args.name: pos
args.doc: pan position, -1 is left, +1 is right

ugens.name: BiPanB2
ugens.doc: Encode a two channel signal to two dimensional ambisonic B-format. This puts two channels at opposite poles of a 2D ambisonic field. This is one way to map a stereo sound onto a soundfield. It is equivalent to: PanB2(inA, azimuth, gain) + PanB2(inB, azimuth + 1, gain)

args.name: azimuth
args.doc: position around the circle from -1 to +1. -1 is behind, -0.5 is left, 0 is forward, +0.5 is right, +1 is behind.

ugens.name: DecodeB2
ugens.doc: 2D Ambisonic B-format decoder. Decode a two dimensional ambisonic B-format signal to a set of speakers in a regular polygon. The outputs will be in clockwise order. The position of the first speaker is either center or left of center.

args.name: numChannels
args.doc: number of output speakers. Typically 4 to 8.

args.name: orientation
args.doc: Should be zero if the front is a vertex of the polygon. The first speaker will be directly in front. Should be 0.5 if the front bisects a side of the polygon. Then the first speaker will be the one left of center. Default is 0.5.

ugens.name: LinPan2
ugens.doc: Two channel (stereo) linear panner. This one sounds more like the Rhodes tremolo than Pan2.

args.name: pos
args.doc: pan position, -1 is left, +1 is right

ugens.name: LinXFade2
ugens.doc: Two channel linear crossfader.

ugens.name: Pan2
ugens.doc: Two channel (stereo) equal power panner.

args.name: pos
args.doc: pan position, -1 is left, +1 is right

ugens.name: Pan4
ugens.doc: Four channel equal power panner. Outputs are in order LeftFront, RightFront, LeftBack, RightBack.

args.name: xpos
args.doc: x pan position from -1 to +1 (left to right)

args.name: ypos
args.doc: y pan position from -1 to +1 (back to front)

ugens.name: PanAz
ugens.doc: Multichannel equal power panner.

args.name: pos
args.doc: pan position. Channels are evenly spaced over a cyclic period of 2.0 with 0.0 equal to the position directly in front, 2.0/numChans a clockwise shift 1/numChans of the way around the ring, 4.0/numChans equal to a shift of 2/numChans, etc. Thus all channels will be cyclically panned through if a sawtooth wave from -1 to +1 is used to modulate the pos. N.B. Front may or may not correspond to a speaker depending on the setting of the orientation arg, see below.

args.name: width
args.doc: The width of the panning envelope. Nominally this is 2.0 which pans between pairs of adjacent speakers. Width values greater than two will spread the pan over greater numbers of speakers. Width values less than one will leave silent gaps between speakers.

args.name: orientation
args.doc: Should be zero if the front is a vertex of the polygon. The first speaker will be directly in front. Should be 0.5 if the front bisects a side of the polygon. Then the first speaker will be the one left of center. Default is 0.5.

ugens.name: PanB
ugens.doc: Ambisonic B format panner. Output channels are in order W,X,Y,Z.

ugens.name: PanB2
ugens.doc: Encode a mono signal to two dimensional ambisonic B-format.

args.name: azimuth
args.doc: position around the circle from -1 to +1. -1 is behind, -0.5 is left, 0 is forward, +0.5 is right, +1 is behind.

ugens.name: Rotate2
ugens.doc: Rotate2 can be used for rotating an ambisonic B-format sound field around an axis. Rotate2 does an equal power rotation so it also works well on stereo sounds. It takes two audio inputs (x, y) and an angle control (pos). It outputs two channels (x, y). It computes this: xout = cos(angle) * xin + sin(angle) * yin; yout = cos(angle) * yin - sin(angle) * xin; where angle = pos * pi, so that -1 becomes -pi and +1 becomes +pi. This allows you to use an LFSaw to do continuous rotation around a circle.

args.name: pos
args.doc: angle to rotate around the circle from -1 to +1. -1 is 180 degrees, -0.5 is left, 0 is forward, +0.5 is right, +1 is behind.

ugens.name: XFade2
ugens.doc: Equal power two channel cross fade

args.name: pan
args.doc: Pan between the two input signals with -1 being inA only and 1 being inB only with values between being a mix of the two.

args.name: level
args.doc: Output level - 0 being silent and 1 being original volume

ugens.name: CoinGate
ugens.doc: When it receives a trigger, it tosses a coin, and either passes the trigger or doesn't.

args.name: prob
args.doc: Value between 0 and 1 determines probability of either possibilities

ugens.name: ExpRand
ugens.doc: Generates a single random float value in an exponential distributions from lo to hi.

ugens.name: IRand
ugens.doc: Generates a single random integer value in uniform distribution from lo to hi

ugens.name: LinRand
ugens.doc: Generates a single random float value in linear distribution from lo to hi, skewed towards lo if minmax < 0, otherwise skewed towards hi.

args.name: minmax
args.doc: Skew direction (towards lo if negative otherwise hi)

ugens.name: NRand
ugens.doc: Generates a single random float value in a sum of n uniform distributions from lo to hi. n = 1 : uniform distribution - same as Rand n = 2 : triangular distribution n = 3 : smooth hump As n increases, distribution converges towards gaussian

ugens.name: RandID
ugens.doc: Choose which random number generator to use for this synth. All synths that use the same generator reproduce the same sequence of numbers when the same seed is set again.

ugens.name: RandSeed
ugens.doc: When the trigger signal changes from nonpositive to positive, the synth's random generator seed is reset to the given value. All synths that use the same random number generator reproduce the same sequence of numbers again.

ugens.name: TExpRand
ugens.doc: Generates a random float value in exponential distribution from lo to hi each time the trig signal changes from nonpositive to positive values lo and hi must both have the same sign and be non-zero.

ugens.name: TIRand
ugens.doc: Generates a random integer value in uniform distribution from lo to hi each time the trig signal changes from nonpositive to positive values

ugens.name: TRand
ugens.doc: Generates a random float value in uniform distribution from lo to hi each time the trig signal changes from nonpositive to positive values

ugens.name: Clip
ugens.summary: Clip a signal outside given thresholds.
ugens.doc: Clip a signal outside given thresholds. This differs from the ugen clip2 in that it allows one to set both low and high thresholds.

args.name: lo
args.doc: Low threshold of clipping. Must be less then hi

args.name: hi
args.doc: High threshold of clipping. Must be greater then lo

ugens.name: Fold
ugens.summary: Fold a signal outside given thresholds.
ugens.doc: Folds input wave to within the lo and hi thresholds. This differs from the ugen fold2 in that it allows one to set both low and high thresholds.

ugens.name: Gate
ugens.summary: Gate or hold
ugens.doc: Lets signal flow when trig is positive, otherwise holds last input value

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

ugens.name: InRange
ugens.summary: Tests if a signal is within a given range
ugens.doc: If in is >= lo and <= hi output 1.0, otherwise output 0.0. Output is initially zero.

ugens.name: InRect
ugens.summary: Test if a point is within a given rectangle.
ugens.doc: Outputs one if the 2d coordinate of x,y input values falls inside a rectangle, else zero

ugens.name: LastValue
ugens.summary: Output the last value before the input changed
ugens.doc: Output the last value before the input changed by a threshold of diff

ugens.name: Latch
ugens.summary: Sample and hold
ugens.doc: Holds input signal value when triggered.

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

ugens.name: LeastChange
ugens.summary: Output least changed
ugens.doc: output whichever signal changed the least

ugens.name: MostChange
ugens.summary: Output most changed
ugens.doc: output whichever signal changed the most

ugens.name: Peak
ugens.summary: Track peak signal amplitude
ugens.doc: Outputs the peak amplitude of the signal so far, a trigger resets to current value

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

args.name: reset
args.doc: Resets the counter to zero when triggered.

ugens.name: PeakFollower
ugens.summary: Track peak signal amplitude
ugens.doc: Outputs the peak signal amplitude, falling with decay over time until reaching signal level

ugens.name: Phasor
ugens.summary: Resettable linear ramp between two levels
ugens.doc: Phasor is a linear ramp between start and end values. When its trigger input crosses from non-positive to positive, Phasor's output will jump to its reset position. Upon reaching the end of its ramp Phasor will wrap back to its start. N.B. Since end is defined as the wrap point, its value is never actually output.

args.name: trig
args.doc: When triggered, reset value to reset-pos (default: 0, phasor outputs start initially)

args.name: rate
args.doc: The amount of change per sample i.e at a rate of 1 the value of each sample will be 1 greater than the preceding sample

args.name: resetPos
args.doc: The value to jump to upon receiving a trigger

ugens.name: Pitch
ugens.summary: Autocorrelation pitch follower
ugens.doc: This is a better pitch follower than zero-crossing, but more costly of CPU. For most purposes the default settings can be used and only in needs to be supplied. Pitch returns two values (via an Array of OutputProxys, a freq which is the pitch estimate and has-freq, which tells whether a pitch was found. Some vowels are still problematic, for instance a wide open mouth sound somewhere between a low pitched short 'a' sound as in 'sat', and long 'i' sound as in 'fire', contains enough overtone energy to confuse the algorithm. None of these settings are time variable.

args.name: initFreq
args.doc: Value of output pitch until first pitch detected.

args.name: execFreq
args.doc: The target rate to periodically execute in cps. Clipped between min-freq and max-freq.

args.name: maxBinsPerOctave
args.doc: Number of lags for course search. A larger value will cause the coarse search to take longer, a smaller value will cause the subsequent fine search to take longer.

args.name: median
args.doc: Median filter value of length median on the output estimation. Helps eliminate outliers and jitter. Value of 1 means no filter.

args.name: ampThreshold
args.doc: Minum peak to peak amplitude of input signal before pitch estimation is performed.

args.name: peakThreshold
args.doc: Finds the next peak that is above peak-threshold times the amplitude of the peak at lag zero. A value of 0.5 does a pretty good job of eliminating overtones.

args.name: downSample
args.doc: Down sample the input signal by an integer factor. Helps reduce CPU overthead. Also reduces pitch resolution.

args.name: clar
args.doc: Clarity measurement (purity of the pitched signal) if greater than 0.

ugens.name: PulseCount
ugens.summary: Pulse counter
ugens.doc: Each input trigger increments a counter value that is output.

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

args.name: reset
args.doc: Resets the counter to zero when triggered.

ugens.name: PulseDivider
ugens.summary: Pulse divider
ugens.doc: Outputs a trigger every div input triggers

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

args.name: div
args.doc: Number of pulses to divide by.

args.name: startVal
args.doc: Starting value for the trigger count. This lets you start somewhere in the middle of a count, or if startCount is negative it adds that many counts to the first time the output is triggers.

ugens.name: RunningMax
ugens.summary: Track maximum level
ugens.doc: Outputs the maximum value received at the input. When triggered, the maximum output value is reset to the current value.

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

ugens.name: RunningMin
ugens.summary: Track minimum level
ugens.doc: Outputs the minimum value received at the input. When triggered, the minimum output value is reset to the current value.

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

ugens.name: Schmidt
ugens.summary: Schmidt trigger
ugens.doc: Outout one when signal greater than high, and zero when lower than low.

ugens.name: SendReply
ugens.summary: Send information via OSC to Overtone
ugens.doc: Send an array of values from the server via an message. The OSC message is formed with cmd-name as the path, followed by two compulsary args: node-id (the id of the node that sent the message) and reply-id (the value specified in the params). These args are then followed by the list of values specified in the params. For example, if the ugen is used as follows: (send-reply tr \"/foobar\" [1 2 3] 42) When the trig tr triggers, Overtone will receive an event that looks like the following (where 32 represents the node-id of the synth that sent the message): {:path \"/foobar\

args.name: cmdName
args.doc: A string or symbol, as a message name.

args.name: values
args.doc: Array of ugens, or valid ugen inputs

args.name: replyId
args.doc: Integer id (similar to that used by send-trig)

ugens.name: SendTrig
ugens.summary: Send a /tr OSC message to Overtone
ugens.doc: On receiving a trigger sends a :trigger event with id and value. This command is the mechanism that synths can use to trigger events in clients. The trigger message sent back to the client is this: int - node ID int - trigger ID float - trigger value This is then presented as an event on the event-stream which is a map containing the key :path with the string \"/tr\" and the key :args containing a sequence of the values in the above order. i.e. {:path /tr, :args (34 3 123.0)} See on-trigger, on-latest-trigger and on-sync-trigger for registering handlers for trigger events.

args.name: id
args.doc: an integer that will be passed with the trigger message. This is useful if you have more than one send-trig in a synth design. Consider using trig-id to genearate a unique id.

args.name: value
args.doc: A ugen or float that will be polled at the time of trigger, and its value passed with the trigger message

ugens.name: SetResetFF
ugens.summary: Set-reset flip flop
ugens.doc: When a trigger is received the output is set to 1.0 Subsequent triggers have no effect When a trigger is received in the reset input, the output is set back to 0.0 One use of this is to have some precipitating event cause something to happen until you reset it.

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

args.name: reset
args.doc: Resets the counter to zero when triggered.

ugens.name: Stepper
ugens.summary: Pulse counter
ugens.doc: Triggers increment a counter which is output as a signal. The counter loops around from max to min by step increments

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

args.name: reset
args.doc: Resets the counter to resetval when triggered.

args.name: step
args.doc: step value each trigger. May be negative.

args.name: resetval
args.doc: value to which the counter is reset when it receives a reset trigger.

ugens.name: Sweep
ugens.summary: Triggered linear ramp
ugens.doc: outputs a linear increasing signal by rate/second when trig input crosses from non-positive to positive

ugens.name: TDelay
ugens.summary: Trigger delay
ugens.doc: Delays an input trigger by dur, ignoring other triggers in the meantime

ugens.name: TWindex
ugens.summary: Triggered window
ugens.doc: When triggered, returns a random index value based on array as a list of probabilities. By default the list of probabilities should sum to 1.0, when the normalize flag is set to 1, the values get normalized by the ugen (less efficient).

args.name: trig
args.doc: Trigger - can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

ugens.name: Timer
ugens.summary: Trigger timer
ugens.doc: Outputs time since last trigger

ugens.name: ToggleFF
ugens.summary: Toggle flip flop
ugens.doc: Flip-flops between zero and one each trigger

ugens.name: Trig
ugens.summary: Timed trigger
ugens.doc: When a nonpositive to positive transition occurs at the input, Trig outputs the level of the triggering input for the specified duration, otherwise it outputs zero.

args.name: trig
args.doc: trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

args.name: dur
args.doc: duration of the trigger output in seconds.

ugens.name: Trig1
ugens.summary: Timed trigger
ugens.doc: Outputs one for dur seconds whenever the input goes from negative to positive, otherwise outputs 0.

args.name: trig
args.doc: trigger. Trigger can be any signal. A trigger happens when the signal changes from non-positive to positive.

args.name: dur
args.doc: duration of the trigger output in seconds.

ugens.name: Wrap
ugens.summary: Wrap a signal outside given thresholds.
ugens.doc: Wraps input wave to the low and high thresholds. This differs from the ugen wrap2 in that it allows one to set both low and high thresholds.

ugens.name: ZeroCrossing
ugens.summary: Zero crossing frequency follower
ugens.doc: Outputs a frequency based upon the distance between interceptions of the X axis. The X intercepts are determined via linear interpolation so this gives better than just integer wavelength resolution. This is a very crude pitch follower, but can be useful in some situations.
